steps.title: Welcome to Voltaj
steps.text: Voltaj is a demo shop on a real AWS architecture in Frankfurt. Use it like a normal shop. The violet parts are the learning layer. The shop itself never uses violet.

steps.title: The Behind the scenes panel
steps.text: Each action adds a numbered call to the panel on the right. Each entry is one real AWS call: the service, the operation, the request, the time, the network path and the cost when we know it.

steps.title: Step badges link to the diagram
steps.text: A badge such as P2 · S3 · 4 means: diagram page 2, scenario 3, step 4. Click the badge to open the architecture diagram at that step.

steps.title: Popular products come from Kafka
steps.text: Your clicks go to Amazon MSK. A consumer group counts the views in DynamoDB. This list reads the counters. Open a product, then come back later: the counts change.

steps.title: Choose a persona
steps.text: A persona is a real Cognito user with an order history. Choose one to use the cart and the checkout. Your own cart stays separate from other visitors.

steps.title: Search runs in OpenSearch Serverless
steps.text: The product function sends a multi_match query to the collection voltaj-search. Then it reads the live price and stock from two DynamoDB tables with one BatchGetItem.

steps.title: Try the fuzzy experiment
steps.text: Search for a word with a typing error, for example hedphones. Turn fuzzy matching off and search again. Compare the request text in the panel.

steps.title: Where does the index come from?
steps.text: Nobody writes to OpenSearch directly. The zero-ETL integration copies each catalog change from the DynamoDB stream to the index. Click 101 on the Search entry to see the document next to the DynamoDB item.

steps.title: One GetItem, one BatchGetItem
steps.text: The page reads the product item from the catalog table, then the price and the available stock. The panel shows the read capacity and the cost of each call.

steps.title: Add to cart
steps.text: Choose a quantity and add the product. The Cognito authorizer checks your token before the cart function runs. A line can have at most 5 pieces: a condition in UpdateItem stops more.

steps.title: The cart is in DynamoDB
steps.text: Each line is one item with the key CART#<persona>~<visitor> and a TTL of 7 days. DynamoDB deletes old carts by itself.

steps.title: Checkout starts a saga
steps.text: API Gateway starts the Step Functions workflow directly, without a Lambda function, and answers at once. The work continues in the background. The panel keeps adding entries.

steps.title: Follow the saga
steps.text: Each step on this page comes from a live trace entry. The workflow reserved the stock in one DynamoDB transaction and created a payment at VoltPay.

steps.title: Pay, decline or wait
steps.text: Open VoltPay. Pay sends a signed webhook and the order continues. Decline or No answer starts the compensation: the stock goes back and PaymentFailed goes to the bus.

steps.title: Events after the response
steps.text: After the confirmation, OrderPlaced fans out: SNS for email and SMS, the order buffer for the 3PL, and the commerce log in Kafka. These entries arrive later, also minutes later for the shipment.

steps.title: Send the same event twice
steps.text: Delivery is at least once. Send OrderPlaced again and watch each consumer stop at its idempotency key.

steps.title: Orders are relational
steps.text: The order function writes orders and order lines to Aurora PostgreSQL in one transaction. It connects through RDS Proxy with a 15-minute IAM token, not a password.

steps.title: Simulated email and SMS
steps.text: SES sends to the mailbox simulator and End User Messaging sends to a simulator number. The calls are real, but no real person gets a message. This page shows what was sent.

steps.title: The admins group and MFA
steps.text: The back office needs a Cognito user in the group admins. The demo admin has a TOTP authenticator. The page computes the code, and the panel shows the MFA challenge.

steps.title: Save a product, then search for it
steps.text: The save is one PutItem. About ten seconds later the zero-ETL pipeline has indexed it. Search for the name to see the change in OpenSearch.

steps.title: Upload an image
steps.text: The browser puts the file directly in S3 with a presigned URL. S3 starts the resize through EventBridge. The new image appears when the resize entry arrives.

steps.title: The analytic side
steps.text: These reports read Step Functions executions, the event log, queue depth, MSK consumer lag, the data lake and the counters.

steps.title: Experiments with limits
steps.text: Break a consumer and redrive the DLQ, replay events from the archive, or send a capped burst. Each experiment has a limit per hour to protect the cost.

steps.title: 101 lessons in Turkish
steps.text: Each lesson explains one pattern for beginners. A lesson opened from a panel entry shows your own call and your own data.
